newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Annan expects Cyprus peace talks at U.N. in June.
newsitem.headline: Annan expects Cyprus peace talks at U.N. in June.

text.p: U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan said on Saturday he would invite the leaders of the Greek and Turkish communities in Cyprus to direct talks on settling their conflict and expected a meeting next month in New York.
"I intend to invite them to New York in June for us to have face-to-face negotiations," Annan told a news conference during an official visit to Moscow.
President Glafcos Clerides, the Greek Cypriot leader, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash had both indicated they were willing to talk, he said.
"I do expect peace talks on Cyprus to begin in New York in the course of the month," he said, adding that the talks would probably be in the second half of the month.
Sir Kieran Prendergast, U.N. under secretary-general for political affairs, said in Nicosia on Friday, after meeting both Cypriot leaders, that the invitation from Annan was likely.
If the talks go ahead it will be the first known encounter between the two leaders in nearly three years.
The United Nations is looking at the idea of the talks rotating between New York and a European venue.

The U.N. and a small army of mediators have been trying to reunite Cyprus under a federal umbrella since 1974, when Turkish troops invaded the north in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece.

It intensified its bid to get stalled peace talks going after the killing of four Greek Cypriots along the U.N. patrolled buffer zone separating the two communities and the fatal shooting of a Turkish Cypriot sentry last summer.
